SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word describes a picture that shows the four cardinal points? (1 mark)
   A. Compass rose
   B. Weather chart
   C. Timeline
   D. Rain gauge

2. Which of these counties has a coast on the Indian Ocean? (1 mark)
   A. Nakuru
   B. Kitui
   C. Kilifi
   D. Nyeri

3. Which is the longest river inside Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Yala River
   B. Tana River
   C. Nzoia River
   D. Athi River

4. What is a mountain? (1 mark)
   A. Very high land with steep sides and a peak
   B. A large body of water
   C. A wide flat area
   D. A low place between hills

5. On a weather chart, which symbol usually means a sunny day? (1 mark)
   A. A sun
   B. A cloud
   C. A wind arrow
   D. A raindrop

6. What is a season? (1 mark)
   A. The weather on one day
   B. A part of the year with a typical kind of weather
   C. A type of crop
   D. A kind of clothing

7. Which of these is one of the four seasons in the county? (1 mark)
   A. Winter
   B. Rainy season
   C. Autumn
   D. Spring

8. Thimlich Ohinga is found in which county? (1 mark)
   A. Nairobi
   B. Migori
   C. Turkana
   D. Mombasa

9. What is a historic built environment? (1 mark)
   A. A natural forest
   B. A new shopping mall
   C. A river
   D. A place built long ago that tells us about the past

10. Which is a way of showing appreciation for others? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring their help
   B. Saying thank you
   C. Laughing at their work
   D. Breaking their tools

11. Why can no person do every job alone? (1 mark)
   A. There are too many skills and jobs to learn
   B. Money is not needed
   C. People are lazy
   D. Jobs are not important

12. What is harambee? (1 mark)
   A. A type of crop
   B. Working together to solve a problem
   C. A kind of market
   D. A school subject

13. Who helps at weddings and funerals in many communities? (1 mark)
   A. Only the government
   B. Nobody
   C. Only the police
   D. Neighbours and relatives

14. Which is the best way to show population on a map using dots? (1 mark)
   A. Colour the whole map blue
   B. Draw dots where people live and give a key for what a dot means
   C. Write the county name only
   D. Draw a river

15. Why must a key be included on a dot map? (1 mark)
   A. So that the map is longer
   B. So that people know what each dot stands for
   C. So that colours are hidden
   D. So that it looks old

16. Which of these is an artefact? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A mountain
   C. A cloud
   D. A clay pot

17. Which festival is held in Lamu? (1 mark)
   A. Nairobi Snow Day
   B. Nakuru Fish Fair
   C. Lamu Cultural Festival
   D. Kisumu Rain Day

18. Which is a way of conserving water? (1 mark)
   A. Turning off taps after use
   B. Cutting trees near rivers
   C. Polluting rivers
   D. Leaving taps running

19. Which is a service industry? (1 mark)
   A. A cement plant
   B. A dairy plant
   C. A sugar mill
   D. A hotel

20. Why should every sale be recorded? (1 mark)
   A. So that money can be checked and accounted for
   B. So that the project fails
   C. So that profit disappears
   D. So that pupils have more homework

21. What does Stop-Think-Share teach? (1 mark)
   A. Post quickly
   B. Think before you post
   C. Share your password
   D. Ignore rules

22. What is a role model? (1 mark)
   A. A machine
   B. A person whose good behaviour others admire and copy
   C. A kind of book
   D. A person who breaks rules

23. What is a duty? (1 mark)
   A. A gift
   B. A game
   C. Something you may not do
   D. Something you are expected to do

24. What is bullying? (1 mark)
   A. Repeatedly hurting or frightening someone weaker
   B. Sharing food
   C. Playing together
   D. Helping a friend

25. What is a right? (1 mark)
   A. A game
   B. Something every person is allowed to have or do
   C. A punishment
   D. A chore

26. What does equality mean in an election? (1 mark)
   A. Some people have many votes
   B. Only boys vote
   C. Each person has one vote of equal value
   D. Only teachers vote

27. Which minister would organise a football match between classes? (1 mark)
   A. Environment
   B. Sports and games
   C. Library
   D. Health

28. In a mock session, what should pupils do first after opening? (1 mark)
   A. Leave
   B. Close the meeting
   C. Read the last minutes
   D. Fight

29. What do clan elders do? (1 mark)
   A. Cook school lunch
   B. Keep customs and settle disputes
   C. Sell tickets
   D. Repair roads

30. What does MCA stand for? (1 mark)
   A. Master of County Affairs
   B. Member of the County Assembly
   C. Mayor of Central Area
   D. Minister of County Administration

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain three elements of democracy and give an example of each in school. (5 marks)

32. State three road safety rules for a rainy day. (3 marks)

33. Give three reasons why economic activities are important. (3 marks)

34. Describe three problems that crowded areas can have and one way of reducing each. (5 marks)

35. Where can a child go for help if they are being harmed? (2 marks)

36. On a sketch map the school is in the middle, the market is above it and the clinic is below it. Write two sentences to say where the market and the clinic are. (4 marks)

37. Describe how an ordinary pupil can support the Children's Government. (3 marks)

38. Explain three effects of child abuse on a child. (3 marks)

39. List the steps for solving a conflict peacefully. (4 marks)

40. Describe the houses of two communities in Kenya. (4 marks)

41. Explain how the four seasons can influence what people do in your county. Give one example for each season. (5 marks)

42. Explain why forgiveness is important for peace. (3 marks)

43. State three things that spoil peace in school. (3 marks)

44. Explain why a Children's Government should not punish pupils. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Compass rose
   A compass rose shows N, E, S and W.

2. C — Kilifi
   Kilifi lies along the coast.

3. B — Tana River
   The Tana River is the longest river in Kenya.

4. A — Very high land with steep sides and a peak
   A mountain is much higher than the land around it.

5. A — A sun
   A sun symbol shows sunny weather.

6. B — A part of the year with a typical kind of weather
   A season is the weather that is typical over several months.

7. B — Rainy season
   The four seasons are hot, cold, dry and rainy.

8. B — Migori
   Thimlich Ohinga is in Migori County.

9. D — A place built long ago that tells us about the past
   Historic built places are old places made by people.

10. B — Saying thank you
   Thanking people shows we value them.

11. A — There are too many skills and jobs to learn
   Nobody can grow all food, teach, heal and build alone.

12. B — Working together to solve a problem
   Harambee means pulling together.

13. D — Neighbours and relatives
   People help by cooking, lending items and comforting.

14. B — Draw dots where people live and give a key for what a dot means
   A dot map needs a clear key.

15. B — So that people know what each dot stands for
   Without a key we cannot read the dots.

16. D — A clay pot
   A clay pot is made by people.

17. C — Lamu Cultural Festival
   The Lamu Cultural Festival celebrates coastal culture.

18. A — Turning off taps after use
   Saving water helps everyone.

19. D — A hotel
   Hotels provide services.

20. A — So that money can be checked and accounted for
   Records show that money was handled honestly.

21. B — Think before you post
   We should think about whether it is true, kind and safe.

22. B — A person whose good behaviour others admire and copy
   Role models set good examples.

23. D — Something you are expected to do
   A duty is a responsibility.

24. A — Repeatedly hurting or frightening someone weaker
   Bullying is repeated unkind behaviour.

25. B — Something every person is allowed to have or do
   Rights protect people.

26. C — Each person has one vote of equal value
   Everyone's vote counts the same.

27. B — Sports and games
   Sports leaders organise games.

28. C — Read the last minutes
   Minutes remind the group of past decisions.

29. B — Keep customs and settle disputes
   Clan elders guard customs and settle quarrels.

30. B — Member of the County Assembly
   MCA is a Member of the County Assembly.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: Equality: one vote each. Freedom of expression: giving opinions in class. Majority rule: choosing a game by most votes. Award marks for each element and example.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct element with example, up to 5.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not cross flooded roads, wear bright or reflective clothes, and walk facing traffic if there is no pavement.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: They provide food, they give jobs and income, and they earn taxes for county services.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: Shortage of houses: build more houses. Litter: organise cleaning and waste collection. Traffic: improve roads and public transport. Award marks for each problem and each solution.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each problem/solution pair, up to 5 marks.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: To a trusted adult such as a parent or teacher, or to the child helpline 116.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct source of help.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: The market is north of the school. The clinic is south of the school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct direction word and 1 mark for each correct sentence.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Vote for leaders, follow fair instructions, and give ideas through the class representative.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pain and illness, fear and sadness, and missing school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each effect.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stop, calm down, talk and listen, find a solution together, and say sorry and forgive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step, up to 4.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: The Maasai build low houses of wooden frames covered with mud and dung inside a fence called a manyatta. Old coastal houses in Lamu were built of coral stone with carved doors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each community and 1 mark for each description.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Rainy: farmers plant crops. Dry: farmers harvest and dry crops. Hot: people drink more water and wear light clothes. Cold: people wear warm clothes and drink hot tea. Award a fifth mark for a clear explanation of why seasons matter for farming.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each season example and 1 mark for the link to activities.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: It ends quarrels, it helps friendships to grow again, and it stops anger from continuing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bullying, fighting and spreading rumours. Accept stealing or discrimination.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Only teachers decide on discipline, pupil leaders may be unfair, and serious problems must be reported to teachers.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.
